style: English psych folk funk, 100 BPM: a deep, dry London bass-baritone with Brixton vowels, cool and unbothered like a seventies soul-jazz street poet narrating over the groove, rich, rounded and unhurried, glottal stops and dropped H's, the verses talked in a laid-back conversational lilt, half-spoken half-sung, talked not rapped, a wry storyteller propped at the pub counter, slow and swaggering, then lighting up with grinning soulful runs and big held notes as hook and bridge arrive, a roomful of pals bellowing the refrain back. Tin whistle carrying the lead above hand drums and congas, a fat head-nodding funk breakbeat and a slinky funk bass. Underneath, a string quartet: plucked pizzicato answering the whistle through the verses, long sweeping bowed lines in the bridge. Psychedelic dub layers: mellotron strings, backwards guitar swells, wah auto-panned wide across the stereo image, spring-reverb guitar skanks, fuzz bass doubling the bassline in the hook, echo-chamber delay throws trailing off line endings. A single operatic tenor soars a wordless high line over the final hook only.
exclude: sitar, tabla, drone, Indian, comedy, novelty, parody, kazoo, cartoon, trap, double-time, fast rap, autotune, EDM, country, smooth R&B, rap, hip hop, boom bap, American accent, screaming, dancehall, ragga, toasting, reggaeton, choir, orchestral bombast
lyrics:
[Intro: tin whistle tune opens the song straight away, congas, breakbeat and funk bass beneath it, mellotron strings fading up, no drone]

[Verse One: cool talked delivery, low and close, string pizzicato replying to each whistle phrase, guitar skanks splashing in spring reverb]
They say, ya can't make money from a tree
let's see, each day, make hay, not free, aay
work and get paid though, earning that dough
but where does it go? nobody knows!

means of production means a reduction
standards bleeding, land-lords needing
quantative easing, grandma FREEEEEEEZING!
stimulus checks are next. Get wrecked!

[Aside: deadpan and unbothered, groove rolls on underneath, echo repeats the final word]
rent seeking?... I'm just about eating
sorry, did I interrupt your meeting?
remember kids, the Fed is not your friend!
it prints all the dollars that the government spends

[Pre-Hook: speech melting into melody, backwards guitar swells, echoes stacking]
this fiat system is insistent
on debts existence, sooooo
don't be hating on the credit rating
or have resistance to the facts I'm stating

[Hook: grinning soul runs and long held notes, the whole pub bellows it back, fuzz bass shadowing the riff, wah sweeping left to right]
Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

[Verse Two: stripped to bass, breakbeat and congas, relaxed talked delivery, pizzicato and whistle trading phrases, echoes at each line's end]
Stacks and stacks of elastic cash
distracted by a dispraxic flash,
mob, angry at their shitty little job
the right and the left both witness the theft

blaming each other is a sick little cover
institutional, dilutional, the usual
distraction IS the attraction
the intention is tension between the factions

divide and conquer, just look at the hand
It's not ya standard, propaganda, worth a couple grand-ahh
it is, state, level, manipulation
it is the devil, with a radio station

[Pre-Hook: speech melting into melody, mellotron climbing, reverb splash]
stack up the vaults like a wheelbarrow
risk of default is really rather narrow
Biggie said waaaay back in ninety seven
don't get high off your own supply

[Hook: grinning soul runs and long held notes, the whole pub bellows it back, fuzz bass shadowing the riff, wah sweeping left to right]
Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

[Verse Three: sly talked delivery, whistle and plucked strings swapping phrases between lines]
You know the real star is Pablo Escobar,
who has elastic bands not plastic hands,
stacking up the cash by the grands
standard plans are for the working man

and this right here is a next level scam
ill gotten gains, no need to explain
"bail" and "out", will never mean the same
own the printer and you don't fear winter

[Bridge: quartet changes to long sweeping bowed lines, backwards guitar swells, voice warms into soulful held notes, building steadily without shouting, echo space opening wide]
crime is asset inflation, passive creation;
of a wealth gap that drives the situation
working people get paid in money, so it's not very funny
when you print more and expect them not to worry

[Final Hook: biggest soulful peak, everyone in the room singing, fuzz bass and breakbeat flat out, one operatic tenor soaring a wordless line high above]
hungry people, feed a revolution,
then it's retribution, perhaps some execution
it's time to give, not just to take
but for heaven’s sake, don't just eat cake

[Outro: whistle, plucked strings and bass, mellotron dissolving, last word echoing into the distance]

[End]
